rationale: Recent bigram-tail variants mostly replayed the output head and kept missing the best score, so this pivots to a new low-cost architecture idea while preserving the winning rank-64 bigram plus projection-only FP16 tail. I added a compile-stable gated carryover path across the deepest decoder blocks, transplanting the stronger hidden state from the start of the tail into later tail blocks with tiny per-channel control tensors that stay high fidelity through the final roundtrip. This is materially different from the failed extra-MLP recurrence: it adds almost no compute or artifact bytes, compounds directly on the current best script, and targets the hidden representation that feeds the already-proven bigram/output tail. I also removed the dead final-calibration path to keep the script lean under the line cap.
title: Gated Tail Carryover On Bigram64 Tail
